answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may post offers or earn reputation. A trellis of referrals can show which accounts vouched for it, while a lantern-style audit flags clusters that repeatedly fund one another; the graph’s shared vertex is evidence, not proof, since legitimate agents may share owners. Sybils then cost the attacker real capital per identity, tied up until the bond is released and forfeitable if fraud is proven.
